title: Official Launch of the Somalia Open Budget Survey 2025
excerpt: The Ministry of Finance and UNICEF launched the Somalia Open Budget Survey 2025 in Mogadishu, putting budget transparency, public participation and oversight in the spotlight.

content:
• Date: 24 November 2026
  • Venue: Decale Hotel, Mogadishu, Somalia
  • Organizers: Ministry of Finance, Federal Government of Somalia, in collaboration with UNICEF

Introduction

The official launch of the Somalia Open Budget Survey 2025 was held on 24 November 2026 at Decale Hotel in Mogadishu. The event was organized by the Ministry of Finance of the Federal Government of Somalia in collaboration with the United Nations Children's Fund (UNICEF).

The launch brought attention to the importance of transparency, accountability, and public participation in Somalia's public financial management system. It provided a platform for stakeholders to reflect on the country's progress in making budget information accessible to citizens and strengthening public engagement in government financial decision-making.

Objectives of the Event

The launch aimed to:

  • Present the Somalia Open Budget Survey 2025 and its relevance to public financial management.
  • Promote transparency and accessibility of government budget information.
  • Encourage meaningful public participation in the national budget process.
  • Strengthen accountability and institutional oversight of public resources.
  • Identify opportunities for improving Somalia's budget transparency and public financial governance.

Key Areas of Discussion

The event focused on three important dimensions of open budgeting:

  • Budget Transparency: Improving the timely publication, accessibility, and comprehensibility of government budget documents so that citizens and other stakeholders can understand how public resources are raised, allocated, and spent.
  • Public Participation: Encouraging citizens, civil society organizations, and other stakeholders to participate meaningfully in budget formulation, implementation, and monitoring.
  • Budget Oversight: Strengthening the role of Parliament, independent institutions, and relevant oversight bodies in ensuring responsible management and accountability for public funds.

Institutional and Development Significance

The Somalia Open Budget Survey represents an important opportunity to assess the country's budget transparency and identify areas requiring further institutional improvement.

Greater openness in public budgeting can contribute to stronger public trust, improved governance, more informed policy decisions, and better alignment between government spending and citizens' priorities.

The collaboration between the Ministry of Finance and UNICEF also highlights the importance of partnerships in advancing transparent and inclusive public financial management.

Conclusion

The official launch of the Somalia Open Budget Survey 2025 represents a significant opportunity to advance discussions on public financial transparency, accountability, and citizen participation in Somalia. Moving forward, sustained institutional commitment, stronger public access to budget information, and meaningful engagement with citizens will be essential to strengthening Somalia's public financial management system.
